provenance: Applied by hand from the examiner rubric in SPEC.md section 4. Not captured from a live model run. See SPEC.md section 7.

verdicts.claim: The warehouse automation market is growing at roughly 23 percent annually and will exceed 51 billion in value within four years.
verdicts.reason: Two precise market figures are asserted with no analyst, filing, or survey named anywhere in the document.

verdicts.claim: Mid-market distributors are the fastest moving buyers in this category because they feel labor cost pressure without the procurement overhead that slows enterprise deals.
verdicts.reason: A comparative claim about buying speed across segments needs cycle-time data the document never offers.

verdicts.claim: Northwind Robotics is positioned to capture the middle of that market, where incumbents price for enterprise and startups build for single warehouses.
verdicts.reason: The competitive shape it rests on is asserted rather than shown, with no pricing or product evidence for either group.

verdicts.claim: The ideal customer operates 3 to 8 distribution centers and moves more than 40,000 units a week.
verdicts.reason: This stipulates the target definition rather than asserting a fact about the world, so it needs no external basis to stand as written.

verdicts.claim: These operators lose roughly 18 percent of picking capacity to labor turnover, which is why automation payback lands inside 14 months for them.
verdicts.reason: A measured capacity loss and a payback period are both stated as settled with no measurement or model behind either.

verdicts.claim: Buying authority sits with the VP of Operations, so the entire motion should route to that title rather than to IT.
verdicts.reason: Buying authority is treated as known while no won-deal record, interview, or org data is cited, and routing the whole motion rests on it.

verdicts.claim: Northwind wins on time to value because deployment takes six weeks against an industry norm of five months.
verdicts.reason: The comparison carries the claim and the five-month industry norm has no source at all.

verdicts.claim: The competitive set has trained the market to expect long implementations, so a fast deployment claim breaks through immediately.
verdicts.reason: A market-wide expectation and its messaging effect are both asserted with no test, survey, or campaign result behind them.

verdicts.claim: Pricing at 4,200 dollars per robot per month will read as premium and will therefore signal quality to this buyer.
verdicts.reason: The price is a decision the document may set, but the buyer perception it predicts is an unsupported claim about people the document never spoke to.

verdicts.claim: Outbound to VP Operations titles will produce a 6 percent reply rate in this segment, well above the 2 percent B2B average.
verdicts.reason: A forecast reply rate three times a quoted benchmark is offered without a single send having been run or a source for the benchmark.

verdicts.claim: Trade shows drive the highest quality pipeline in industrial categories, so Northwind should anchor the year on three regional logistics events.
verdicts.reason: A superlative across an entire category is asserted with no channel comparison, and a year of budget is committed on it.

verdicts.claim: A partner motion through systems integrators will eventually contribute 40 percent of new revenue.
verdicts.reason: A specific revenue share is projected for a motion that does not yet exist and has produced no data.

verdicts.claim: The plan produces 120 qualified opportunities in the first year.
verdicts.reason: The number is stated as an outcome rather than a target and no conversion arithmetic or historical rate is shown to reach it.

verdicts.claim: Win rate should reach 22 percent once the deployment story is proven in two reference accounts.
verdicts.reason: A win rate is forecast from a condition that has not occurred, with no prior win rate given to anchor it.

verdicts.claim: That combination delivers 8.4 million in new annual recurring revenue by the end of year one.
verdicts.reason: It is derived from an opportunity count and a win rate that both collapsed, so the revenue figure inherits their emptiness.
